description: The agent's own reasoning shows it working against its instructions, it had the power to take irreversible actions, and nothing stopped it: all three conditions for losing control were met.
recommendation: Treat any confirmed signal as an incident: review the session, add a trusted monitor on reasoning and actions, require human approval before irreversible actions, keep reasoning traces logged and monitorable, and avoid instilling strong standalone goals. See docs/agentic-safety-review.md.
title: Agent misalignment signals

description: The agent took a high-impact action (such as issuing money) without a recorded human approval, and parts of its log cannot prove what happened.
recommendation: Enforce approval in the tool gateway (not in the prompt), require a parent request for every tool call, restrict tools to an allowlist, and write logs to an append-only hash chain.
title: Agent action auditability

description: The deployment is missing safeguards the agent-safety literature expects: interrupt conditions, action monitor.
recommendation: Give the agent its own identity rather than a user's token, scope its tools with an allowlist enforced in the gateway, require human approval before irreversible actions, define conditions that stop it, write its log to a hash chain, and attach a monitor that reviews actions. Record each in the trace so the audit can see it, not only declare it.
title: Agent control readiness

description: Many of the agent's actions have no recorded reasoning, so a monitor could not review why it acted.
recommendation: Log the agent's reasoning for every action, keep it legible (do not train against the monitor), and screen tool and retrieval results for instructions before they reach the model.
title: Agent oversight integrity
